content.value_statement: Android teams need interfaces that match platform expectations and scale across devices. This skill gives Material 3 and Jetpack Compose guidance for practical mobile UI work.
actual_capabilities: Explains Material Design 3 principles for Android app interfaces.
Provides Jetpack Compose layout patterns for lists, cards, forms, and navigation.
Shows Material 3 theming with dynamic color, typography, and shape guidance.
Covers bottom navigation, drawers, deep links, and adaptive navigation.
Highlights accessibility practices such as touch targets and content descriptions.
References official Android and Material resources for deeper implementation work.
limitations: Does not compile or test Android projects by itself.
Uses illustrative sample code that may need project-specific imports.
Does not replace Android release notes or app store policy review.
Requires developer judgment for architecture, data flow, and state management.

use_cases.title: New Compose Screen
use_cases.description: Create a Material 3 screen layout with correct spacing, typography, and component choices.

use_cases.title: Design System Update
use_cases.description: Translate brand colors and typography into Material 3 themes and responsive components.

use_cases.title: Navigation Review
use_cases.description: Check whether screens use bottom bars, drawers, and deep links in expected Android patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Android Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Jetpack Compose screen for a task list app. Include Material 3 components, spacing, states, and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Component Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Android component plan for cards, buttons, text fields, and lists. Suggest Material 3 improvements and missing states.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Adaptive Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design navigation for a phone, tablet, and foldable Android app. Compare bottom navigation, rail, drawer, and deep link behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Compose Design System
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Compose design system for Material 3 theming, dynamic color, typography scale, accessibility, and reusable component boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a profile screen for an Android finance app.
output: Recommended structure using a top app bar, profile header, settings list, and confirmation dialogs.
Material 3 component choices with state and accessibility notes.
Responsive adjustments for compact and expanded widths.

output_examples.input: Our app needs navigation across home, search, favorites, and profile.
output: Bottom navigation for compact phones, with saved state and single top behavior.
Navigation rail guidance for expanded screens.
Deep link considerations for product and profile destinations.

output_examples.input: We need a Material 3 theme for a branded Android app.
output: Color scheme guidance using primary, secondary, tertiary, surface, and container roles.
Dynamic color recommendations for Android 12 and later.
Typography and shape guidance for reusable Compose components.

best_practices: Start with MaterialTheme color, typography, and shape before styling individual components.
Use adaptive navigation patterns based on screen width and task frequency.
Check content descriptions, contrast, touch targets, loading states, and error states.
anti_patterns: Copying sample snippets without adapting state, imports, and architecture.
Using one phone layout for tablets, foldables, and landscape screens.
Hardcoding colors or sizes instead of using Material 3 design tokens.

faq.question: Does this skill write Jetpack Compose code?
faq.answer: It provides Compose patterns and examples. You still need to integrate and test code in your Android project.

faq.question: Does it cover Material Design 3?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers components, color roles, dynamic color, typography, shapes, and Android interaction patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with Android navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes bottom navigation, drawers, navigation rail guidance, arguments, and deep link examples.

faq.question: Can it test my app?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest UI structure and review patterns, but it does not run Android builds or tests.

faq.question: Is it only for developers?
faq.answer: No. Designers can use it to align Android screens with Material 3 and Compose constraints.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains local guidance and reference links. The links are optional resources for manual reading.
